'''The Cairns''' was a region of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. The [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as [[the Dead Road]] traveled through the region.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I remembered looking at the map in the back of ''The Lord of the Rings'' and wondering about the parts of Mordor Frodo and Sam never visited, and tried to summon up that feeling. Hence a minor trade route became the Dead Road, and a region of Hutt Space became the Cairns.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Suvudu">{{Suvudu|url=2009/08/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-mapping-hutt-space.html|text=STAR WARS: THE ESSENTIAL ATLAS &ndash; Mapping Hutt Space}}</ref>}}
The Cairns were introduced in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', a [[2009]] reference book co-authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]]. The book placed the region in grid squares T-10 and T-11.<ref name="TEA" /> In a 2009 article published on [[Unbound Worlds|Suvudu]], Fry noted that the creation of the Cairns was inspired by a map included with<ref name="Suvudu" /> [[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien's]] novel<ref name="Tolkien">{{WebCite|url=https://harpercollins.co.uk/pages/tolkien|text=The Lord of the Rings Archives|work=[https://www.tolkien.co.uk HarperCollins Publishers UK]|archivedate=20220118132632}}</ref> [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings|''The Lord of the Rings'']]. The map in question illustrated the land of [[Wikipedia:Mordor|Mordor]], including areas not visited by the novel's protagonists [[Wikipedia:Frodo Baggins|Frodo Baggins]] and [[Wikipedia:Samwise Gamgee|Samwise Gamgee]].<ref name="Suvudu" />
